anzsic_codes.name: Other Auxiliary Finance and Investment Services

merger_description:
EQT Holdings Limited (**EQT**, and together with its subsidiaries, **EQT Group**) has agreed to acquire Platinum Investment Management Limited (**PIML**), a subsidiary of L1 Group Limited (**L1**, and together with its subsidiaries, **L1 Group**) (the **Acquisition**).

PIML is the responsible entity for a number of registered managed investment schemes operated by L1 Group. Following completion of the Acquisition, EQT Group will be the responsible entity for these registered managed investment schemes and L1 Group will remain as the investment manager.

EQT is a financial services provider that offers, among other things, corporate trustee services (including corporate responsible entity services) and investment/asset management services.

L1 is an ASX-listed, global investment manager formed in 2025 through the merger of L1 Capital and Platinum Asset Management.

PIML trades as Platinum Asset Management and is a financial services provider that offers, corporate trustee and investment/asset management services, acting as the responsible entity and investment manager for all of the Australian registered managed investment schemes of the Platinum Asset Management business.

events.title: Notification waiver determination published

determination_table_content.details:
In making this notification waiver determination, the Australian
Competition and Consumer Commission (the ACCC) has considered
the information provided with the notification waiver application and
had regard to the factors in section 51ABV(2)(b) of the Competition
and Consumer Act 2010 (Cth) (the Act).
Based on the information provided in the application, the ACCC
considers that the Acquisition is unlikely to give rise to any material
lessening of competition given:
a. there is very small horizontal overlap between EQT and PIML
in the supply of responsible entity services to customers in
Australia, given PIML provides these services solely for L1
Group
b. there are alternative suppliers of responsible entity services
in Australia.
In these circumstances, the ACCC does not consider it necessary to
reach a concluded view on the likelihood of the notification
thresholds being met.
Given that material competition concerns are unlikely to arise, the
ACCC has determined that the Acquisition is not required to be
notified.
The ACCC considers that the determination is consistent with the
object of the Act and the interests of consumers in promoting
competition.
For more information about the ACCC’s approach to considering
notification waiver applications and to assessing competition
effects more generally, see the ACCC’s guidance on notification
waivers and merger assessment guidelines.
